quotes.text: Learn how to migrate to the 3.0.0 of the Stripe Terminal SDK.

old_evidence.text: After we enable the changes in the backend for your account, you must disconnect and reconnect to your reader using the SDK for the updated configuration to take effect.
If `connectReader` fails, your integration needs to make a new call to `discoverReaders` to resume discovering readers.
The parameters for these methods haven’t changed but the error types have also been renamed to `SCPConfirmPaymentIntentError` and `SCPConfirmRefundError` respectively.
The reader status will now remain `CONNECTING` while installing any required updates.
Only the name of the method is changed, the behavior of these methods remains identical.

findings: The November canonical capture is a migration-title and two-platform navigation index. It verifies the iOS and Android variant links and v3.0.0 purpose. It contains no migration steps or variant behavior.

The May 1, 2026 historical guide describes existing pre-3.0.0 iOS and Android SDK migrations. iOS v3 needs iOS 13+, Android v3 needs Android 8/API 26+, compared with the respective 2.x iOS 11+/Android API 21+ floors. SDK discovery changes to reader-type configs, process calls move to confirm names, and readReusableCard is removed in favor of the SDK create/collect/confirm SetupIntent sequence.

The May iOS guide says cancellation reports SCPErrorCanceled, discovery completes at connectReader invocation, a failed connection requires another discovery call to resume discovery, and a previously discovered reader can be passed to connect without ongoing discovery. Busy errors move to an internal command queue. Builder error handling differs in Swift and Objective-C, and the reconnection delegate receives the reader.

May places Android permission checks at discovery. Location applies to any discovery config and Bluetooth only to BluetoothDiscoveryConfiguration. Bluetooth or USB stays CONNECTING during a required update and reports connected and ready after successful completion. Android Serializable guidance applies to Parcel access and recommends against persistence across SDK versions.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The prior May 1 capture remains the full evidence for v3.0.0 and its platform minima, despite a 2025 filename suffix. The historical offline private-preview sequence is Stripe backend account enablement, then SDK reader disconnect/reconnect. Offline-created PaymentIntent stripeId on iOS and id on Android can be null.

The Android list removes reader/listener/capture/configuration fields and redirects fingerprints to server-side SDKs. Preserve the historical two method renames and iOS renamed error types separately. Use separate current SDK or offline guides for newer-version rules.
conflicts: The summary's 'only rename, behavior unchanged' wording applies the Android evidence to iOS. The May iOS section explicitly preserves parameters and also renames both error types. Qualify the language independently of the November index.

The mapped summary omits historical offline enablement and reconnection qualification and states CONNECTING without Bluetooth/USB scope. Capture those boundaries without using a historical private-preview notice to assert current access.
unresolved_questions: The November index gives no content for the current iOS/Android variants and no evidence of changed v3 API, device minima, or contemporary offline availability.

findings: Link the November iOS/Android variant index and keep May as the behavior-bearing raw. Preserve the existing reciprocal Terminal concept, labeling its source link as historical v3 and routing current integration guidance separately.
Correct the cross-platform rename claim and add the dated offline account-enablement and reconnect conditions. Specify Bluetooth/USB for Android's required update readiness transition.
conflicts: No November functional evidence supersedes May. The iOS error types and old private-preview conditions are independent corrections to the existing summary.
source_assessments.reason: The index adds navigation to the two platform variants. The prior full capture supplies useful existing-summary corrections, chiefly the iOS error names and offline scope.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/references/sdk-v3-migration-guide, source-stripe-terminal-sdk-v3-migration-guide should use the November 7 capture only as navigation. It identifies Terminal SDK 3.0.0 migration and links iOS and Android variants. It contains no developer instructions or runtime transitions (new raw lines 5-14). The May 1 guide tells pre-v3 developers to move to iOS 13+ or Android API 26+ and use per-type discovery configuration. Historical offline payment access required Stripe backend enablement followed by SDK disconnect/reconnect, and offline PaymentIntent IDs can be null (old raw lines 12-44, old raw lines 73-85, old raw lines 101-119, old raw lines 133-145). On iOS, discovery now ends when connectReader starts, can report cancellation as SCPErrorCanceled, and must be invoked again to resume discovery after a failed connection. A previously discovered reader can still be reused. Commands queue instead of producing SCPErrorBusy, and the reconnection delegate receives the reader (old raw lines 46-71). Android checks Location at discovery and requires Bluetooth permissions only for the Bluetooth discovery config. A Bluetooth/USB reader with a required update stays CONNECTING until the update completes successfully (old raw lines 121-131). Both rename the payment/refund process methods and recommend create/collect/confirm SetupIntents instead of readReusableCard. Android calls the renames behavior-identical. iOS says parameters are unchanged and its two confirmation error types also change, which the current summary should preserve (old raw lines 89-95, old raw lines 155-167).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/references/sdk-v3-migration-guide, add a raw_reference from source-stripe-terminal-sdk-v3-migration-guide to the November 7 iOS/Android variant index. This is a capture/navigation change from the full May 1 historical guide. The two variant links establish no new v3 behavior, feature removal, or general current access (new raw lines 9-14, old raw lines 8-25, old raw lines 97-119). Keep May as authority for the v3 platform floors, SDK discovery permission timing, required-update readiness gate for Bluetooth/USB, and offline historical private-preview/account enablement, disconnect/reconnect and null-ID behavior (old raw lines 14-19, old raw lines 25-31, old raw lines 73-85, old raw lines 101-107, old raw lines 121-145). The old summary's blanket 'only rename' claim uses Android wording and obscures iOS's renamed errors SCPConfirmPaymentIntentError and SCPConfirmRefundError. Retain unchanged iOS parameters with the renamed errors and keep Android's identical method behavior and Parcel serialization qualification separate (old raw lines 89-95, old raw lines 155-167). Preserve the stripe-terminal reciprocal route as historical SDK v3 and the separate SDK and offline guides for newer integration decisions.
